host.binding: numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0 (all 48 CPUs of the single NUMA node)

command.startup: dive --version | dive parse docs/user/examples/Counter.tla | dive check docs/user/examples/Counter.tla --config docs/user/examples/Counter.cfg --workers 1 --seed 0 --fp 0 --output json (50 fresh runs each)
command.validation: dive validate-trace <module.tla> --config <model.cfg> --trace trace.json --seed 0 --fp 0 --output json (10 each); --sample for 100 bosco simulation traces (simulate --traces 100 --depth 100 --seed 0)

deviations: The 100 --sample traces come from bosco's simulation, not MCLamportMutex's: MCLamportMutex simulation stops at its first trace with a reported deadlock, so it yields one trace.
Release binary built on one bench node and copied to the others, because independent builds of the same source were not byte-identical; dive_binary_sha256 names the copied binary.
timing: perf_counter around subprocess.run; check, simulate and validate-trace under GNU /usr/bin/time -v for peak RSS

specifications/lamport_mutex/MCLamportMu.result: violation (simulation deadlock on the first trace)
specifications/lamport_mutex/MCLamportMu.note: Every successor of the trace's last state is pruned by the state constraint, which dive reports as a deadlock (docs/user/simulation.md). The run stops after one trace, so it is not a throughput figure.

specifications/bosco/bosco.cfg.note: Rates use stopped.elapsed_ms (the budget clock). Peak RSS from time -v is about 1.8x the --max-memory limit: the budget samples process memory during simulation; publication of the retained traces happens after the stop. Tracked in the D5 perf issue.
